newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania urges EU not to split new entrants.
newsitem.headline: Romania urges EU not to split new entrants.

text.p: Romania implicitly criticised the European Union's decision on Tuesday to limit discussions on eastward expansion to six countries, saying any enlargement in waves would be "artificial and discriminatory".

Government ministers said the EU move excluding Romania was no more than a recommendation to be confirmed later this year. But they admitted the country had to proceed with reforms to enable the economy to adapt to membership.
In a statement sent to the EU ahead of the Commission's decision at a meeting in Strasbourg, the government said all candidates should begin talks on membership at the same time.

"We believe an enlargement strategy of waves should be avoided. This would create new demarcations which would divide the candidate states in an artificial and discriminatory way," the statement said.
"It would be desirable for talks to start simultaneously with all candidate states. The status of a full member should be acquired as soon as all criteria for admission are met."

The Commission announced in Strasbourg that Poland, the Czech Republic, Hungary, Slovenia and Estonia should join Cyprus in entry talks. Remaining candidates, including Bulgaria, Latvia, Lithuania, Slovakia and Romania, were left to prepare for membership at their own pace.
Integration Minister Alexandru Herlea said the move was "not a decision, but rather a recommendation by the commission. The decision will be taken in Luxembourg in December."
He said Romania had to work hard to meet EU demands.
"The integration process depends on us and how we proceed with tough reforms and with strengthening democratic institutions," he said.
The government statement also urged the EU to examine progress in economic reforms since the election nine months ago of a centrist government after seven years of leftist rule.
The decision had been all but a formality after commissioners last week settled differences over how many east European countries would be invited to enlargement talks.

Trade and Industry Minister Calin Popescu Tariceanu said he expected Romania would win EU membership within six to seven years. "In the meantime, Romania can make the necessary economic progress," he told state television.

The Commission's ruling was issued a week after NATO limited its initial eastward expansion to Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic, leaving Romania on the sidelines despite a determined last-minute campaign for early inclusion.
